claim: In the HA community discussion, the moderator-endorsed Linux options for an official-companion-like experience are glances, netdata, system bridge, and system monitor — no official Linux companion app existed as of Dec 2024.
stance_target: there is a real unmet gap for a proper Linux HA agent; ha-linux-agent addresses an officially-unfilled niche
scope_conditions: HA Community 'Month of WTH' thread, Dec 2024; moderator 'Tinkerer' (DubhAd on GitHub) reply #2
quoted_support: For Windows do check out https://github.com/LAB02-Research/HASS.Agent For Linux you've got glances, netdata, system bridge, and system monitor.

claim: HASS.Agent depends on MQTT for most of its functionality — without MQTT only Quick Actions work — although it can connect to HA via API (long-lived token) for basic operations.
stance_target: MQTT is the load-bearing bidirectional transport for command execution in existing desktop agents; ha-linux-agent's MQTT choice matches the incumbent architecture
scope_conditions: HA community thread, user Protoncek (HASS.Agent user) reply #6, Dec 2024
quoted_support: You don't have to have MQTT to use HASS.Agent; however, most features rely on it for bidirectional communication. Without MQTT, only Quick Actions will work.

claim: The macOS HA app's low support cost is explained by it running the iOS companion app, so a bespoke Windows/Linux companion would need dedicated developers — an HA moderator notes 'All that needs is some Windows developers to step up and create it'.
stance_target: no official Linux companion is coming from HA itself; the Linux agent niche must be filled by third-party projects like ha-linux-agent
scope_conditions: HA community thread Dec 2024; Participant (HA dev/participant) reply #11 and moderator reply #10
quoted_support: Part of the reason is that MacOS is able to run the iOS companion app… I don't want to say it comes for "free", but the effort to support is much lower versus a bespoke app for Windows or Linux.

claim: Community participants state the differentiating value of a companion app over a browser is device sensors, and a 'native package to push sensor readings (and maybe execute local commands) over to HA' would suffice even without a GUI.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's core value proposition (headless sensor reporting + local command execution) matches what the community explicitly asked for
scope_conditions: HA community thread, replies #11 and #19, Dec 2024
quoted_support: Honestly, if it were just a native package to push sensor readings (and maybe execute local commands) over to HA, it'd be totally fine to still need a browser to view the interface.

claim: Mosquitto is available as an official Home Assistant addon, and a community member argues MQTT integration is 'more native than many things' in HA despite user resistance to MQTT.
stance_target: the position that MQTT is a non-native/inferior integration path for a Linux HA agent (from the same thread's original poster)
quoted_support: Native way… well, 70% of things in HA aren't "native way"… (like hacs etc…) so it's definitely more native than many things (at the end mosquitto is official addon)
